sample_unit: variant observations (200 consecutive tumor NGS cases; 1228 unique variants)

links.outcome: Concordance of LLM variant classification with historical laboratory classifications on local clinical cases
links.effect: Mean concordance with historical interpretation 97.5% (range 97.4% to 97.6%) across three replicates; 42 variants (2.9%) discordant in at least one replicate.
links.quote: Across three replicates, mean concordance with historical interpretation was 97.5% (range, 97.4% to 97.6%).

links.outcome: Reproducibility of LLM classifications across repeated runs
links.effect: Three replicates gave 97.4% to 97.6% concordance; most discordances were consistent across runs, reflecting interpretive ambiguity rather than model instability.
links.quote: Discordances predominantly reflected intrinsic interpretive ambiguity, evidence evolution, and rule stringency rather than model instability.

unlisted_practices: Rule-constrained LLM using explicit gene-specific expert guidance files to structure prompts for somatic variant classification
Blinded post hoc expert adjudication of discordant variants
Cross-model replication with a different LLM

screen.reason: Evaluates the diagnostic accuracy and concordance of a novel rule-constrained LLM framework (OLIVE) for somatic variant interpretation on retrospective clinical cases.
